title: A Marionette Above the Stage
description: Look behind a small puppet performance through strings, a control bar, and the figure moving below them.
cardDescription: Look behind a small puppet performance through strings, a control bar, and the figure moving below them.
focus: A marionette is controlled from above using strings or wires. Other puppet forms use hands or rods, so the clues specify the arrangement rather than applying it to every puppet.
solvingTip: Separate the figure from its controls and the theater space surrounding it.
words: Puppet moved from above by strings or wires
Thin line connecting an overhead control to the puppet
Hand-held frame directing a marionette's attached lines
Movable connection between parts of a puppet's body
Person operating the figures in a puppet performance
Small performance area seen by the audience
Operator's body part holding the control frame
Upper body part of the puppet figure
Movable limb attached beside the puppet's torso
Lower limb lifted during a walking movement
Fabric screen opening onto the puppet scene
Small object used by the puppet character
One part of the miniature performance

answerNotes.MARIONETTE: A marionette uses an overhead control system, unlike a hand puppet operated from inside.
answerNotes.STRING: Strings transmit the operator's movements; their placement influences which parts move.
answerNotes.CONTROL: The control is held above the figure; it is not the puppet's visible body.
answerNotes.JOINT: Joints allow limbs to bend, while strings provide the pulling action.
answerNotes.PUPPETEER: A puppeteer creates the movements; performers can use several different puppet techniques.

title: Shadows Behind a Theater Screen
description: Explore a shadow performance through a light source, cut-out figures, and the dark shapes seen by the audience.
cardDescription: Explore a shadow performance through a light source, cut-out figures, and the dark shapes seen by the audience.
focus: A shadow performance uses a light and an intervening figure to create an outline. The audience sees the resulting silhouette rather than all the surface details of the object making it.
solvingTip: Distinguish the light source, the blocking figure, and the surface receiving the shadow.
words: Dark outline of a figure seen against a brighter background
Blocking visible light from passing directly through
Surface on which a shadow performance is displayed
Flat shaped figure used to cast a recognizable shadow
Side-view outline of a face or figure
Dark region produced where a figure blocks light
Controlled figure used in the performance
Illumination needed to make the shadow visible
Device supplying the light behind the figures
Thin control supporting or moving a shadow figure
Body part that can itself form a shadow shape
Directed path of light from a source
Flat vertical surface usable as a simple shadow screen
Outline distinguishing one shadow character from another

answerNotes.SILHOUETTE: A silhouette shows an outline rather than the object's full internal detail.
answerNotes.OPAQUE: An opaque figure casts a shadow by blocking light; a translucent screen can pass scattered light.
answerNotes.SCREEN: The screen receives or reveals the shadow image; it is separate from the light source behind the figures.
answerNotes.CUTOUT: A cutout's outline helps create the image even when its surface markings are unseen.
answerNotes.PROFILE: Profile describes a viewing direction rather than the material making the shadow.

title: Rehearsing a Community Play
description: Follow a theater rehearsal through scripts, stage positions, and the short words used to coordinate a scene.
cardDescription: Follow a theater rehearsal through scripts, stage positions, and the short words used to coordinate a scene.
focus: A rehearsal prepares a performance through repeated work. The clues distinguish a spoken line, an entrance signal, and a person helping the cast remember the text.
solvingTip: Read whether the clue concerns words, movement, a role, or a location beside the stage.
words: Practice session preparing a play for performance
Person helping a performer recall a forgotten line
Person guiding a play's interpretation and stage action
Written dialogue and directions used to prepare the play
Signal for a performer to speak or make an entrance
Group of actors taking the play's roles
Character part assigned to an actor
One portion of dialogue learned by a performer
Section of action within a play
Area where the actors rehearse their movements
Concealed space beside the acting area
To leave the visible acting area
Object handled by an actor during a scene
To perform a rehearsal sequence continuously

answerNotes.REHEARSAL: A rehearsal develops timing, words, and movement before the public performance.
answerNotes.PROMPTER: A prompter supplies a reminder; the director coordinates the larger artistic work.
answerNotes.DIRECTOR: A director works with the cast and production team rather than necessarily appearing as a character.
answerNotes.SCRIPT: The script supplies text and directions; the performance also involves movement, sound, and interpretation.
answerNotes.CUE: A cue marks timing, while the spoken line is the text delivered afterward.

title: Costumes in the Theater Wardrobe
description: Explore a theater’s clothing collection through fitting work, fabric pieces, and accessories worn by performers.
cardDescription: Explore a theater’s clothing collection through fitting work, fabric pieces, and accessories worn by performers.
focus: A costume helps establish a character’s appearance. The clues separate a worker’s role from a garment and from the construction details that make a costume fit.
solvingTip: Use the part’s function: sewing, fastening, covering, or helping a performer change.
words: Theater department or collection responsible for costumes
Theater worker helping performers put on and change costumes
Clothing worn by a performer to represent a character
Session checking and adjusting how a costume sits on its wearer
Template guiding the cutting of costume fabric
Cloth used to make a stage garment
Folded finish along a costume's lower edge
Stitched join between pieces of garment fabric
Artificial hair worn as part of a character's appearance
Head covering chosen for a stage character
Shoulder-hung costume garment leaving the arms free
Face covering used in some theatrical roles
Small pointed fastener used during a costume fitting
Sleeveless garment worn over a shirt

answerNotes.WARDROBE: Wardrobe names the costume collection or department here, not a bedroom furniture item.
answerNotes.DRESSER: A dresser assists with garments and changes; the same word can name furniture in another context.
answerNotes.COSTUME: A costume supports characterization rather than merely describing an actor's ordinary clothes.
answerNotes.FITTING: A fitting concerns garment fit and alterations before use on stage.
answerNotes.PATTERN: A sewing pattern guides construction; it is distinct from a decorative printed fabric design.

title: Lights Above a Small Stage
description: Recognize theater lighting equipment through focused beams, colored filters, and controls used during a performance.
cardDescription: Recognize theater lighting equipment through focused beams, colored filters, and controls used during a performance.
focus: A lighting design separates direction, intensity, and color. The clues describe equipment and effects rather than electrical installation work.
solvingTip: Match the shape of the light or the job of the control to the term.
words: Stage lamp producing a directed concentrated beam
Lamp spreading light over a broad area
Patterned insert used to shape a projected stage-light image
Control adjusting the intensity of a compatible stage lamp
Traditional term for a colored filter placed in a stage-light beam
Light-producing unit in a theater fixture
Arrangement or installation of overhead stage-lighting equipment
Lens type giving a stage light stepped circular zones
Optical part directing a theatrical lamp's beam
Timed instruction to change the lighting during a scene
Directed bundle of light aimed at the acting area
Hue selected for a stage-light effect
To adjust a light's aim or sharpness
Area receiving less illumination than its surroundings

answerNotes.SPOTLIGHT: A spotlight emphasizes a selected area rather than broadly lighting an entire surface.
answerNotes.FLOODLIGHT: A floodlight provides broad coverage; a spotlight provides a more concentrated beam.
answerNotes.GOBO: A gobo can create a pattern by controlling the light passing through an optical system.
answerNotes.DIMMER: A dimmer changes brightness; it is separate from a colored filter or a shaped projection insert.
answerNotes.GEL: Gel is a filter name in lighting, not a food ingredient or hair product in this setting.
